'''David Challinor''' (1920–2008) was an American [[biologist]], [[Natural history|naturalist]], and  Assistant Secretary for Science at the Smithsonian.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Pearce |first=Jeremy |date=2008-03-24 |title=David Challinor, Conservationist, Dies at 87 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/03/24/us/24challinor.html |access-date=2026-09-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sullivan |first=Patricia |date=2008-03-18 |title=Smithsonian Official David Challinor, 87 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/2008/03/18/smithsonian-official-david-challinor-87/a2b7c6d6-c95a-435b-a10d-aad012d80569/ |access-date=2026-09-05 |work=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> His papers are archived at the Smithsonian.<ref name="SIA archives">[http://siarchives.si.edu/collections/siris_arc_302304 David Challinor] at the SIA archives.</ref><ref name="SIA archives 2">[http://siarchives.si.edu/collections/siris_arc_282096 Further David Challinor] at the SIA archives.</ref>

He was an undergraduate at Harvard in the 1940s, and did graduate work at Yale receiving a PhD in 1966, after which he joined the Smithsonian.<ref name=":0" />
